Retrieval misses.rule: answerable item whose anchored chunk is not in the final top 5 (4 with no gold document at all)
Retrieval misses.cause: Reranked top 5 favours sibling chunks or a neighbouring document: for R2-AMT-02 (minimum amount) the rates-and-fees page was outranked by overview/eligibility pages; for R2-DLR-05 (delete my data) Bajaj's privacy/app T&C outranked the RBI consumer-finance direction. No collection router, and both collections compete for 5 slots. Most misses still answered correctly from a sibling chunk (Faithfulness stayed 1.0).

Unfaithful or unsupported claims.cause: Over-strong paraphrase of qualified policy text: 'up to 36%' stated as exactly 36% (R2-LHR-05), exceptions dropped in the digital-lending disbursal rule (R2-DLR-01), 'dropline limit' turned into 'outstanding limit' (R2-PRE-05). No figure was invented outright in the 149 judged answers.

Wrong abstain or refuse.rule: over-abstained on an answerable item (3), refuse/abstain item judged wrong (0), clarify item with no clarifying question (5)
Wrong abstain or refuse.cause: Clarify items: the policy prompt has no instruction to ask a clarifying question, and the intent classifier/clarify logic of the full agent was not exercised, so 10 of 11 vague questions got a direct answer (e.g. R2-CLA-03, R2-CLA-08). Over-abstain: the deterministic request guards fire on benign policy questions: 'my friend and I took the same loan' -> other_applicant (R2-RAT-07) and 'credit guarantee scheme fee' -> guarantee (R2-FEE-08); R2-PUR-01 abstained because no passage states per-purpose limits. All 10 refuse and 8 abstain items were handled acceptably by the judge's rubric.

Hindi and Telugu failures.rule: hi/te item with a failure tag (other than leaked labels) or a metric below its bar (hi 5/9, te 5/11; wrong script: 1)
Hindi and Telugu failures.cause: No wrong-script answers (20/20 in the right script). The few hi/te failures are the same causes as English: a retrieval miss on the RBI-IOS FAQ (R2-LHI-06), a qualified '36%' stated flatly (R2-LHR-05), and conflict notes not made (R2-LHI-03). Samples are small (9 hi, 11 te).

Conflict-note handling.rule: answer_note (conflicting-source) item with ExpectedBehaviour < 1.0, of 11 such items
Conflict-note handling.cause: The POLICY prompt asks to flag [historical] passages but not to surface disagreeing current sources, so the model gives one figure (e.g. ₹75 lakh in R2-AMT-01) without noting the ₹55 lakh conflict; 10 of 11 answer_note items were scored below 1.0.

Latency or rate-limit fallbacks.rule: generator fell back to gpt-5.6-terra on 0 items []; generator gave no answer on 0; judge fell back on 0 metric calls (0 items); agent guard fallback template on 3 items; Groq calls: 0; generation latency per item p50 5.88 s, p95 10.54 s, max 18.59 s (OmniRoute, includes the agent's one rewrite when it happened)
Latency or rate-limit fallbacks.cause: No Groq call is made in this eval (OmniRoute stand-ins), so the Groq-to-OmniRoute fallback never fired. Judge stalls happened when in-flight OmniRoute calls hung after sandbox suspension; the judge was re-run in resumable chunks with a 60 s client timeout, and one metric call fell back to gpt-5.6-terra.

Internal labels shown to the borrower (a.rule: answer text contains an internal term or passage label (leak regex)
Internal labels shown to the borrower (a.cause: The policy prompt asks for citations as P1..P5 labels, and the model also writes them (and the word 'passages') into the answer text; the agent's citation pipeline maps labels to sources but nothing strips them from the prose. Mostly 'passages'/'P1'; 4 answers say 'bureau'.
